newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks close lower on MSCI index news.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks close lower on MSCI index news.

text.p: Jakarta stocks closed lower but off earlier lows on Thursday as investors reshuffled their funds after an announcement on the composition of the new Morgan Stanley Index (MSCI), brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 1.60 points, 0.24 percent, to close at 650.46 points, recovering slightly after falling to 646.46 points.
Decliners led advancers by 65 to 56, with 61 counters unchanged. Total volume was estimated at about 581.6 billion rupiah.
"Today's trading was mixed with reports of the MSCI affecting overall market sentiment," an analyst with a foreign firm said.
She expected the market to continue being mixed on Friday with possible profit-taking in counters which made gains on Thursday.
Brokers and analysts said stocks included in the new MSCI index such as blue chips Bank Negara Indonesia, toll road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala and conglomerate Bimantara Citra recorded gains.
Bank Negara Indonesia was the most active stock with about 67.3 million shares traded, rising 150 rupiah to 1,500 rupiah.

Reports that MSCI will change cigarette firm Gudang Garam's market capitalisation factor from 1.0 to 0.4 had prompted a large sale of the stock, brokers said. It closed 7.35 percent lower at 9,450 rupiah on a volume of four million shares, after plunging to a low of 9,275 rupiah earlier.
Vivi Simampo, an analyst with Danareksa Sekuritas, said the reduction was significant but the fall provided an opportunity for buying.
"In terms of fundamentals, Gudang Garam is a good stock. It performed very well in 1996 and I believe it will continue to perform strongly in 1997," Vivi said.
Analysts said the heavy selling in Gudang Garam might be because the shares was traded at a premium.
It traded at 23 times 1997 earnings compared to the market average of 14 times 1997 earnings.
